name: CableDyn
short: Mooring line and dynamic power cable dynamics, coupled to OpenFAST.
description: A solver for the dynamics of mooring lines and dynamic power cables on floating offshore wind turbines and substations, written in Fortran 2018. It handles lazy-wave cables and taut, semi-taut and catenary moorings, and runs inside OpenFAST as a mooring module (CompMooring = 5). Its accuracy and stability are checked against benchmark cases.

name: CableXSec
short: Cross-section mechanics and fatigue of dynamic power cables.
description: A Python library for the cross-section mechanics of dynamic power cables. It computes the stick–slip of the helical armour wires and the hysteretic bending that follows, the stresses in every wire and component, contact and fretting, temperatures, and the fatigue damage of the armour, conductor and sheaths. It reads the results of global analyses from CableDyn, RIFLEX and OrcaFlex, and exports a hysteretic bending law for use in global analysis.

name: VANE
short: Linearisation and modal analysis of OpenFAST models.
description: A Python library that runs OpenFAST linearisations over a range of operating points and processes the results: mode identification, Campbell diagrams with damping, and state-space models for digital twins, with system identification by a Kalman estimator. It is tested against the four OpenFAST reference turbines.

name: FOWCON
short: Gain-scheduled LQR controller for floating offshore wind turbines.
description: A gain-scheduled LQR controller for floating offshore wind turbines, built as a DISCON controller library, that takes structural damage into account.

name: ISUM
short: Differentiable ultimate strength analysis in JAX.
description: A differentiable implementation of the Idealised Structural Unit Method in JAX, for ultimate strength and progressive collapse analysis of ships and offshore structures. Element equations are derived by automatic differentiation, so ultimate strength can be differentiated with respect to scantlings and material properties. It is under verification against closed-form solutions and the Nishihara and Dow tests.

name: pyBModes
short: Blade and tower mode shapes for OpenFAST.
description: A Python finite element library for the modal analysis of wind turbine blades and towers. It reads OpenFAST, BModes and WindIO input files and writes the mode-shape polynomials ElastoDyn needs. On six benchmark cases it agrees with the BModes Fortran solver to within 0.01 per cent.

name: pyIECWind
description: Generates IEC 61400-1 wind-condition files for the OpenFAST InflowWind module, reproducing NREL’s IECWind tool as a Python library and command-line program.

name: OpenFAST, ROSCO and TurbSim syntax highlighting for VS Code
description: This extension provides syntax highlighting for OpenFAST input files and ROSCO controller input files in Visual Studio Code.

name: pyULSAN
short: Hull girder ultimate strength to IACS CSR-H.
description: Computes the ultimate bending capacity of a hull girder cross-section by the incremental-iterative method of the IACS Common Structural Rules (CSR-H), Part 1, Chapter 5, Appendix 2, together with its elastic and plastic section properties. It also handles heeled bending, strength envelopes and damaged sections. It is a desktop application with user, theory and verification manuals.

name: OpenFAST GUI
short: Desktop application for setting up OpenFAST models.
description: A Python desktop application for setting up and checking OpenFAST and TurbSim models, with a three-dimensional view of the assembled model. It is being written for the graduate course on offshore wind energy.
